newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Bank of China signs US$300 mln FRN issue.
newsitem.headline: Bank of China signs US$300 mln FRN issue.

text.p: The Bank of China on Friday signed a US$300 million floating rate note issue that represented the state-owned commercial bank's first foray into international capital markets in more than two years.

Zhang Guo Wen, executive vice president and managing director at Bank of China's head office, said the strong market response to the issue reflected international investors' support for China as well as for the Bank of China.

"The success of the issue reflects the belief that the international reputation of the Bank of China and of China continues to improve and that China's economic reform and development has begun to create international confidence," he said.
The note issue, launched and closed on Wednesday, has a final maturity of seven years but can be called by the issuer after five years.
It pays a coupon of 37.5 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate and a discount margin of 41 basis points.

Morgan Stanley International and Bank of China International were lead managers. The issue was the first in which Bank of China International, Bank of China's London-based investment banking subsidiary, participated as a joint lead manager.
Twenty banks in addition to the joint leads participated in the transaction in management roles.
Oliver Jury, vice president at Morgan Stanley International, said about 60 percent of the Bank of China note issue was placed in Asia, with the remainder sold to European investors.
Since the notes have been free to trade, the price has improved to 99.88 from 99.80 at launch, he said.
Bank of China's Zhang said the bank has tapped international debt markets some 23 times in the past, with about 10 of these issues denominated in yen.
He said the bank was likely to raise funds again "but when, in what currency and with what instrument will depend on our funding requirements and capital market conditions."
Proceeds of the US$300 million floating rate note will be used to partially finance energy exploration, Zhang said.
